newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Opposition planes bomb Kabul, Taleban advance.
newsitem.headline: Opposition planes bomb Kabul, Taleban advance.

text.p: Warplanes belonging to an anti-Taleban alliance bombed the Afghan capital of Kabul at dawn on Sunday in the second such raid in 48 hours, while Taleban forces were reported to have made gains in overnight fighting north of the city.
Residents of Kabul awoke to a deafening anti-aircraft barrage as Taleban gunners fired on two jets flying high over the city.

The planes dropped at least three bombs, but it was not immediately clear where they fell or whether they had caused any casualties or damage. Most previous raids have targeted Kabul airport, located on the northeastern edge of the capital.

Taleban forces fought through the night in the vicinity of Jabal-os-Siraj, a strategic town about 70 km (44 miles) north of Kabul, gaining more ground, according to the Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) news service.
AIP said the Taleban had killed at least 27 fighters loyal to former government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood and captured 80. Four Taleban were killed and several wounded.
It said the fighting had put the Taleban in control of an area containing five villages east of the Salang highway.
Masood controls the Salang Pass north of Jabal-os-Siraj, as well as his native Panjsher Valley northeast of the town.
Sunday's raid on Kabul followed one on Friday night, when an opposition jet dropped two bombs on the airport. One landed in the air defence section, killing at least one Taleban fighter.
Taleban officials said there was no damage to the runway at the airport, which is used by military and civilian aircraft.

The air strikes appeared to be retaliation for last week's Taleban bombing raids on Maimana, capital of the northeastern province of Faryab, held by forces loyal to northern opposition leader General Abdul Malik.
A spokesman for Malik, General Humayun Fauzi, said on Friday that Taleban raids had killed 90 people in Maimana within 48 hours, including 40 Taleban prisoners held in the city jail.
Fauzi said two Taleban officials, Foreign Minister Mullah Mohammad Ghous and Civil Aviation Minister Maulvi Akhter Mohammad Mansoor were among 30 wounded in the raids.
But an independent military source said there had been no casualties in the bombing of Maimana.
The Taleban, who captured Kabul in September, are fighting to impose their strict Islamic rule across Afghanistan, but have failed to quell opposition forces in the north.
